inputs.good: Synthetic test-only squares: one block of 2,000 and a second package of 66 elsewhere (scene tests).
difficult: zp1-geojson-kml-csv.zip from the run 4 rehearsal: nyc-footprints-2100.geojson read for its bounds only
(2,100 footprints, lon -74.0034 to -73.9402, lat 40.7000 to 40.7999, about 5.3 km by 11.1 km, centres in 24
different 1 km cells). Mirrored in a synthetic test of the same shape.

firstPackage: The area view framed every drawn feature (base map plus every building that ever arrived), not the package.
For the rehearsal case that box is the whole 5.3 by 11.1 km spread: the 1 km bar was 70 px, so 14.3 m per
pixel, and a 20 m candidate ghost covered about 1.4 px. Test on bf9bccbc: 1.98 px per 20 m footprint; a
block package inside a 6 km area base spans 5 percent of the view.
secondPackage: Proven: the capture is the engine's starting pose. Camera (112, 88, 134), 194 m from the target, is 0.176 m
per pixel on the 632 px canvas, which the scale draws as 20 m at 113 px, as in the screenshot; its canvas
hash f1f0bad5 equals the part-1 capture taken before anything drew. Any arrival frames a fresh view at once,
so none of the 66 features had reached that scene when it was captured twice. Proven in the same path:
within one map a second package never framed itself, because the union of all arrivals stayed inside the
earlier frame (test on bf9bccbc: the second package spans 1.6 percent of the view). Not decidable from the
kept evidence: whether the captures came before the area read (5 s poll) or the second package's map read
did not include them. No CRS or local-origin mix-up is involved: framing reads drawn bounds only.

fix: The scene frames the shown package's own drawn features (ids passed by the map from proposalPackageId) with
the area fit's 10 percent margin. When the whole package is wider than 80 typical footprints it frames the
densest window of that size, so footprints stay readable (11.5 px per 20 m footprint on the rehearsal
shape). A new package moves the view to itself with an eased flight.
officerCamera: A pointer down or a wheel on the map, or a selection, stops following. A pointer or wheel also marks the
officer's camera as kept for every later package until a new import starts streaming.
onBase: All 4 scene tests fail on bf9bccbc's engine on their framing assertions (no-op stubs for the two new names).
